mr_title: Renamed permissions upon model renaming in migrations.

expected_issues.title: RenamePermission queries the default database instead of the migrated one
expected_issues.description:
RenamePermission computes `db = schema_editor.connection.alias` but queries ContentType and Permission on the default database, so renames run against the wrong database in multi-database migrations.

Migrations are applied per database alias. The operation reads the alias into `db` yet uses ContentType.objects.filter(...) and Permission.objects.filter(...) without .using(db), so when migrating a non-default database the permissions of the default database are renamed (or none are found), leaving the migrated database inconsistent. The router/alias must be honoured for every query in the operation.

expected_issues.title: Substring model matching renames unrelated model permissions
expected_issues.description: Renaming Book also selects content types such as Notebook in the same app because model__icontains is a substring lookup. Their permissions are rewritten with the new Book model suffix, breaking authorization checks for unrelated models. Match the exact old model name.

expected_issues.title: Model rename overwrites custom permission codenames
expected_issues.description: Every permission for a matching content type is rewritten from its first underscore-delimited token. A custom permission publish_special becomes publish_<newmodel>, losing its application-defined codename and display name. Multiple custom permissions sharing a prefix can also collide. Limit automatic rewriting to recognized generated model permissions, preserving custom permissions.
